title: Burst satiation controller and per-tenant utilization mapper
author: Aisha Park
description: Context: Tenant burst models at scale were causing long-tail capacity contention even when overall cluster utilization was within targets. Existing burst token pools did not account for temporal satiation (a tenant over-consuming repeatedly in short epochs) which led to noisy eviction cycles and degraded p99 latency for best-effort workloads. Motivation: provide a controller that (1) detects and dampens repeated burst hunger per-tenant (satiation), (2) exposes a smoother per-tenant utilization mapping for autoscaling decisions, and (3) emits bounded, low-cardinality telemetry that operations can use for SLA reconciliation and chargeback. This PR introduces the 'satiation controller' and an accompanying 'utilization mapper' that together improve fairness and stabilize autoscaler signals. Design summary: - Satiation controller: tracks tenant burst consumption as an exponentially-weighted satiation score (alpha tunable per-tenant profile). When a tenant's score exceeds a profile-dependent threshold, the controller applies a soft drawdown that reduces burst token replenishment rate for that tenant for a decay window. This is different from hard quota enforcement — it smooths behavior while avoiding abrupt rejections. - Per-tenant utilization mapper: a rolling-window mapper that converts raw GPU occupancy and request-side observed throughput into a normalized utilization metric used by the autoscaler. The mapper reports both a short-window (30s) and long-window (10m) percentile-based utilization (p50/p95) to capture both microbursts and sustained load. Mapping uses sample weighting to prefer recent samples but protects against single-request noise by percentile aggregation. - Telemetry & cardinality control: to avoid high-cardinality metrics, the mapper emits per-tenant aggregated tags only for tenants flagged as 'paying' or 'trial-instrumented' and otherwise funnels detailed traces to the event store sampled at 1%. Aggregated metrics include: tenant_id (hashed bucket), satiation_band (OK/WARM/COOLDOWN), short_p95_util, long_p95_util, burst_replenish_rate. Implementation notes: - runtime/controller/satiation_controller.go: new control loop with light-weight in-memory ledger (bounded to 10k tenants via LRU). The ledger persists minimal state to etcd for leader failover. - controlplane/autoscaler/mapper.go: new mapper with percentile reservoir per-tenant using P^2 algorithm to minimize memory. - api/tenant_profiles.proto: added profile fields (satiation_alpha, cooldown_seconds, replenish_rate_base) with backwards-compatible defaults. - telemetry/metrics_transformer: new aggregation stage that hashes tenant_id into 128 buckets and attaches non-identifying tags. - e2e/test_satiation.py + unit tests for P^2 mapper + CI fixtures. Rollout plan: staged rollout via canary: 1) deploy controller in passive mode (no drawdown) for 24h in canary region, compare p99 latencies and autoscaler churn metrics; 2) enable drawdown for 10% of dedicated fleet; 3) expand to 50% after 48h if no regressions; 4) global enable with monitoring playbooks in place. Metrics to watch: cluster-wide p99/generation latency, dedicated-node eviction count, autoscaler scale events/minute, tenant satiation band distribution, and token pool average utilization. Backout plan: controller runs with a feature flag. Reverting the flag restores previous behavior immediately; persistent state expiry is bounded by cooldown_seconds per profile to avoid long-term effects. Testing: unit test coverage for mapper and controller logic, synthetic canary load tests exercising repeated bursts and mixed workloads, telemetry validation asserting that cardinality remains <= 128 buckets in production traffic sample. Related: ENG-1984 (autoscaler signal noise reduction), ENG-2041 (tenant-level fairness experiments).
commit_summary: feat(satiation): add satiation controller loop and ledger persistence
feat(mapper): implement P^2 percentile mapper and short/long window exposers
chore(proto): extend tenant_profiles.proto with satiation fields
perf(telemetry): add hashing-based aggregation and 1% sampling for detail streams
test(e2e): synthetic canary workload and unit tests for mapper/controller
docs: add operational runbook and rollout checklist
review_comments: Miguel Ortega: Can we make the default cooldown_seconds conservative (>= 300s) to avoid oscillation? Also please add a rollout experiment ID to telemetry for equal comparison.
Aisha Park: Agreed on default; bumped to 600s and added rollout_experiment_id tag. Also added a doc section about expected effects on token pool utilization.
Ravi Kapoor: Mapper looks good; one nit: prefer a decaying sampling weight rather than hard 1% for detailed streams to capture initial-onboarding anomalies. Tests please.
Aisha Park: Implemented decaying sampling: 5% for first 10k requests per tenant, then asymptotes to 1%. Added unit tests and CI fixture.
Dana Li: Verified etcd persistence handles leader failover in local sim; please ensure the ledger LRU limit is observable via metrics.
Aisha Park: Exposed metric runtime.satiation.ledger_size and added alert for >80% of configured capacity.
release_notes: satiation controller: smoother handling of consecutive tenant bursts, new per-tenant utilization mapper (short and long window percentiles), telemetry aggregation to control metric cardinality, and rollout runbook. Improves p99 stability and reduces autoscaler churn in mixed-burst workloads. Backwards-compatible proto additions.
